answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must lock stake in a cryptographic vault before issuing work. Registering multiple identities triggers superlinear cost scaling: creating identity n burns a quadratic stake, forcing attacker cost to scale quadratically O(n^2). Even if a malicious cluster acts like a walnut shell concealing fraudulent entities, the surging tide of burning requirements makes coordinating a plume of phantom nodes economically fatal.
